Q: Java Thread: Real world Application Example A:

@Kayaman commented:

It can be done, but it would be a very poor example of multi-threading.

Here's why.

The unit of useful work that can be done in parallel is (in essence) converting the integers in the lists into strings. That is non-trivial ... but still relatively small.

Against that, you need to need to weigh the overheads of implementing parallelism. These include:

  • The overheads of creating and starting the Thread objects1 that will do the computations that are parallelized, along with the thread pool / executor service that will manage them.

  • The overheads of dispatching work to the threads.

  • The overheads of retrieving the results from the threads in the required order.

(Note that the thread and thread pool setup overheads can be amortized if you are going to print multiple lists. But your problem statement doesn't say there are multiple lists.)

Finally, the process of outputting the strings cannot be parallelized. Java output streams and buffered output streams are synchronized objects. Mutexes are used to stop overlapping write (etc) operations that might result in corrupted output.

If you take all of these in to account, your example is not a good use-case for multi-threading.

Please refer to other answers for examples of how to use multi-threading to solve this problem ... bearing in mind that it doesn't really "help".

1 - Java 21+ virtual threads are not designed for this kind of problem.

Q: Why does Float'Succ behave differently on Float-variables than on Float-expressions? A:

Right. I was replying only to your implied question about the type of Pi. I don't know why GNAT gives these results. I suspect it's because floating-point types are declared in terms of decimal digits (GNAT's Float is digits 6), but implemented in terms of FPU-defined binary mantissae, which generally have greater precision than needed for the digits given (GNAT's Float is implemented with a 24-bit mantissa, which is adequate for digits 7). This implies that Pi is converted to 6-digit precision when assigned to a Float object, but directly to Float'Base when used as a parameter to 'Succ. It also implies that the conversion to Float is optimized away. But I have no way to test this. When I have time I will try your example with ObjectAda to see what it gives.

LATER: I tested your original code with ObjectAda and got similar results to GNAT.

Q: Why textAlign: 'justify' increases letter spacing in some rows A:

In 2026:
On Android textAlight: 'justify' stretches only the whitespaces (at least if there are some, not sure what it does if there is just one long string in a line).

On iOS it still equally stretches the distance between every single letter.

Adding Hyphenation helps a lot in many cases, by breaking down these very long word into shorter peaces, thus filling up lines better.

Would be great to somehow have a the option to configure, whether everything should be stretched or only whitespaces. I'm sure in some cases people even specifically want to stretch not only whitespaces.
